references.text: The prophet Isaiah describes a vineyard that God tends to, but which ultimately yields bad grapes. This resembles the parable Jesus tells in Mark 12:1-9, where the owner of the vineyard sends servants and finally his son, but they are mistreated or killed. Both illustrate God's people who do not listen to His messengers.

The prophet Hosea warns Israel and Judah about their unfaithfulness to God through a parable about an unfaithful wife. This can be seen in connection with how God's messengers, mentioned in Mark 12:5, were treated by the people, showing their unfaithfulness to God.

Jesus tells a similar parable about a vineyard in Matthew, where the owner of the vineyard sends his servants and finally his son to the tenants, who mistreat and kill them. This parallels the events described in Mark 12:5.

Luke also gives a version of the parable about the vineyard owner, who sends several servants and finally his son to the tenants, who mistreat and kill them. This is parallel to the description in Mark 12:5.
